findings.issue: Attempt-2 test replacement - is the strengthened output-fingerprint test meaningful and non-vacuous?
findings.summary: Strengthened test is meaningful and non-vacuous; fingerprint/RenderVersion exclusion is still proven
findings.detail: ChangingVerbosityDoesNotChangeTheProductionRegenerationDecision drives the real production path: it builds two PluginConfigurationSnapshot values that differ only in LogVerbosity, computes ArtworkRegenerationPlanner.ComputeDesiredFingerprint for both over the same identity/metadata/retained source, and asserts equality; it then sets the published state's fingerprint to the warning-derived value and runs ArtworkRegenerationPlanner.Decide for both snapshots, asserting ShouldGenerate is false and DesiredFingerprint is null for each. If verbosity ever entered the renderer configuration fingerprint, the output policy, the badge definitions, or RenderVersion, the trace desired fingerprint would differ and either the equality assertion or the trace Decide assertion would fail. Non-vacuity is independently established by the existing ArtworkRegenerationPlannerTests (ChangedSourceFingerprintGenerates asserts ShouldGenerate=true when the fingerprint changes) and by Phase6OutageTests, so the production gate does return Generate on a fingerprint change. ChangingVerbosityDoesNotChangeTheRendererConfigurationFingerprint is retained, so the configuration-fingerprint exclusion is still directly asserted. The removed request-fingerprint assertion is subsumed: RenderFingerprint.ComputeRequestFingerprint is the output fingerprint plus item/surface, so an unchanged output fingerprint implies an unchanged request fingerprint. The dropped RenderVersion assertions were tautological (RenderVersion.CurrentRendererVersion is a const); the new test passes RenderVersion.CurrentRendererVersion through the production planner, whose Decide compares it with the committed state's RendererVersion. Test count is unchanged at 26.
